messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER: GarnetCorp (privnet) experiencing elevated 502/503 errors hitting NLB -> ALB path for model-serving pool. Service impact: ~30% request failures reported. Paging oncall.
jamie-oncall: Acknowledged. I’m on it. jamie-oncall taking incident lead. Can we get a quick impact summary and recent changes? @taylor-se-garnet please confirm customer visible symptoms.
taylor-se-garnet: Customer reports intermittent inference failures and high tail latency since ~14:22 UTC, retry storms on their side. They see 502s from our edge and timeouts from backend. They asked if we can fail over to dedicated pool.
riley-netops: Looking at NLB metrics: spike in 502/503 error_count + target health flips. TargetGroup arn:arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:...:targetgroup/garnet-models/abc shows 2/4 unhealthy. ALB logs show connection reset by peer, upstream 503 from target instances.
morgan-sre: I pulled audit logs — there was a terraform apply at 14:19 UTC touching security-group sg-0garnet-models that removed an egress rule to internal model-pool subnet (10.23.0.0/20:443) accidentally. Change author: infra-ci (pipeline). Rolling back now would be fastest.
jamie-oncall: Good find. Is the rollback safe? Any risk of oscillation or config drift?
morgan-sre: Rolling back the SG rule is low-risk. I can reapply the previous rule: ingress from NLB subnet -> targets tcp/443, and egress to model-pool on 443. Doing manual fix to be immediate, then follow up with terraform correction.
riley-netops: While morgan re-adds SG rule, we should prepare traffic shift in case targets don't recover. Options: 1) weight DNS (garnet.priv.redwood) -> shift to fallback dedicated pool; 2) disable targets in target-group to force NLB to stop sending; 3) temporarily route via standby ALB.
jamie-oncall: Execute mitigation plan: Step A - morgan, re-add SG rule immediately. Step B - riley, prepare DNS weight change + pre-warm fallback target group. Step C - jamie, notify customer and coordinate failover if no recovery in 5m.
morgan-sre: Re-applying SG rule now (manual edit in console for immediate effect). Command used: aws ec2 authorize-security-group-ingress --group-id sg-0garnet-models --protocol tcp --port 443 --cidr 10.23.0.0/20
morgan-sre: Done. SG rule restored at 14:25:12 UTC. Monitoring target health.
riley-netops: Pre-warming fallback pool: spinning up standby nodes in dedicated pool (runbook: RUNBOOK-PRIVNET-FAILOVER v2). Starting deploy cmd: ./scripts/provision-fallback --customer garnet --count 3
riley-netops: Also set NLB target draining on problematic targets to reduce error surface: aws elbv2 deregister-targets --target-group-arn <tg-arn> --targets Id=i-0aa1,Id=i-0bb2
jamie-oncall: Customer informed: "We're applying emergency mitigation: restoring internal networking and preparing a failover to a dedicated pool if needed. We'll update in 5 minutes." :white_check_mark:
taylor-se-garnet: Customer acknowledged and is on standby. They asked for ETA — gave 5-10m.
morgan-sre: Health checks started returning healthy at 14:26:05 UTC. TargetGroup healthy 4/4 now. Error rate trending down. Rolling back draining on targets.
ellie-support: Monitoring customer telemetry — 502 rate dropped from 32% -> 6% over 2 minutes. No new paging from customer.
jamie-oncall: Excellent. Keeping incident open for monitoring and RCA. Actions: - root cause: unintended SG change from infra-ci pipeline - immediate fix: manual SG restore - mitigations to add: guardrail in pipeline, alerting on SG diffs, canary for TF applies - customer compensation check with Sam.
sam-product: Noted. I'll prepare a short customer summary and compensation options; will sync with sales later.
jamie-oncall: Handoff: I am handing off to morgan-sre for monitoring for the next 60m. If errors resurface, escalate back to paging. Incident severity S2. Incident doc: https://internal.redwood/incidents/1767777777 (auto-created). incident-bot: Incident record created: INC-1767777777, severity=S2, responders=[jamie-oncall,morgan-sre,riley-netops].
incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Incident resolved to degraded state. Monitoring continue. Close window set for 60m. Postmortem owner: morgan-sre. Runbook link: RUNBOOK-PRIVNET-FAILOVER v2.
